newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Midwest hogs trade mixed - private.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Midwest hogs trade mixed - private.

text.p: U.S. Midwest cash hogs traded mixed early, with firm prices in a few areas where meat packers need hogs for Saturday slaughter operations, livestock sources said.
A few packers planned a single Saturday shift. Trade estimates for Saturday slaughter ranged from 45,000 to 85,000 head, which compares with 53,000 a week ago.

Interior Iowa/southern Minnesota sources said packers need to buy hogs for Saturday kills. Early trades were steady-firm at $55.00 per cwt at country points and $56.00 to $56.50 at plants but higher prices were likely later, they said.

Illinois sources reported light marketings there because many producers were deer hunting, but hog prices were weak due to packers having immediate slaughter needs satisfied. Deer season began Friday in Illinois.
Early Illinois trades were steady to weak at $53.50 to $54.50 at country points and $55.00 to $55.50 at plants.

Indiana sources reported steady to lower trades of $53.50 at plants and $52.00 to $52.50 at country points because local packers were not planning a Saturday slaughter. Also, a temporary shutdown at one local plant Thursday resulted in hogs being carried over to Friday.
